title: Introduce lightweight OTEL proxy + adaptive sampling and metric cardinality hygiene
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our OpenTelemetry collector and instrumentation pipeline have accumulated ad-hoc attribute emission and high-cardinality metric labels over the last 18 months. At peak load this manifests as elevated OTEL-collector memory (observed 2.1-2.6GB per replica), CPU spikes during bursty traffic, and noisy dashboards that obscure real SLO regressions. This ticket implements a two-part approach: 1) a thin OTEL proxy (sidecar or ingress proxy) that normalizes, strips, and batches telemetry before the collector; 2) adaptive sampling + metric label hygiene to reduce cardinality and CPU in the backend.
updates: 2025-01-14: Investigation complete — root causes: (a) many services emit request headers and long identifiers as span attributes; (b) collector's resource processors retain full attribute maps; (c) metrics ingestion sees unbounded tag values from request_id-like labels.

2025-01-22: PoC proxy implemented (Go) that performs: attribute allowlist/denylist, truncation of long string attributes, and prefix-based tag bucketing. Local load tests: proxy reduced average OTEL payload size by ~38% and lowered collector ingestion memory by ~30% on the microbenchmark.

2025-01-30: Benchmarked adaptive sampling strategy (rate-limited head-based + tail-based sampling for errors). On a synthetic replay of production traces (50k req/s scaled down), adaptive sampling dropped event ingest volume by 65% while preserving >95% of error traces for SLO diagnostics.

2025-02-06: Metrics hygiene audit completed across 14 services. Identified 9 high-cardinality labels (e.g., full_email, request_path) and recommended replacement with hashed buckets or coarse enums. Implemented guards in proxy to rewrite request_path -> path_bucket.
2025-02-12: PRs open: internal/telemetry:proxy (draft) and infra/helm:collector-config (WIP). End-to-end integration tests added to smoke pipeline.
2025-02-20: Canary plan approved by SRE: rollout proxy to 10% of production traffic for 48 hours with trace sampling set to conservative mode. Observability dashboards and alerts templates updated.
2025-02-21: Memory regression on sidecar seen during canary on one service (leak traced to redis client in proxy). Patch merged and canary resumed.
Next steps: complete code cleanup, add more unit tests, finalize collector config for adaptive sampling and aggregation, and schedule full rollout in runtime-1.22 window.
comments: PM (Mateo Rivera) 2025-01-15: Align on SLIs and acceptable ingestion reduction. Agreed: target 50-70% reduction in noise while preserving error traces.
SRE (Jin Park) 2025-01-28: Please include circuit-breaker and backpressure metrics from the proxy into existing dashboards. Otherwise LGTM.
Design (Rohi Sinha) 2025-02-03: Dashboard changes requested to surface 'discarded attribute' counts per service to help debug regressions after rollout.

Code review (internal/telemetry:proxy) 2025-02-10: Reviewer (Anika Bose) requested clearer config schema and a migration strategy for services already depending on attribute keys. Added feature gate 'otel.proxy.enable_rewrites'.
SRE postmortem note 2024-11-12 (linked): High-cardinality metrics contributed to slow queries during incident INC-2024-11-12. This work mitigates recurrence.
